title: Trace Economics — sprint brief & standup capture (week of 2027-06-07)
content:
Purpose: capture the week’s signal about trace volume growth, dashboard fatigue, and cost telemetry experiments. This is a working capture — lots of hypotheses and TODOs.

Quick summary:
- We saw a ~28% week-over-week increase in spans ingested from the inference fleet (primarily from redwood-serving-prod region eu-west-2). Root cause appears to be both a change in LLM request fanout (new internal transformer routing) and a recent client SDK version that started instrumenting token-level span tags.
- Cost telemetry: token-level tags have exploded cardinality and are now the dominant driver of trace indexing costs. Raw projection: if unchanged, projected extra spend ~+$12k/mo.
- Dashboards: several route-level dashboards are slow and rendering many series with high-cardinality labels. UX feedback: product SREs are blinded by noise during incidents.

Standup notes (daily highlights):
Mon 2027-06-07:
- Diego: started filter to strip token-level tags at the ingestion layer for clients that opt-in. Prototype using a fast regex-based tag dropper. Observed initial 40% drop in index keys on staging traces.
- Priya: dashboards triage — created a quick guardrail template to limit heavy cardinality dimensions to 'top-10 by count' for render.
- Action: add a non-disruptive toggle in the tile config to apply the guardrail.

Tue 2027-06-08:
- Omar: ran a tail-sampling experiment (1% -> 2%) targeted at background long-running traces (inference-dev batch jobs). Early results: ingest volume down 6% in batch namespace, minimal change in alert noise.
- Maya: correlated billing spike to a small set of routes that were tagging every token with 'source_ip' and 'session_id'. Raised OBS-824.

Wed 2027-06-09:
- Infra: discovered an expired cert in the log forwarder causing intermittent replays; cost bump attributed to repeated re-index attempts. Fix deployed; follow-up: runbook update required.
- Priya + Sofia: prototype a pre-aggregation job to compute span-duration histograms at ingest and store as a metric — reduces need to materialize thousands of spans for latency heatmaps. Caveat: introduces 90s aggregation window, acceptable for mid-SLO dashboards.

Thu 2027-06-10 (sync):
- Decision to disable token-level tag ingestion for non-enterprise customers by default (see Decisions section). Implementation plan: feature-flag at the collector, rollout in three waves (staging -> canary -> global).
- Diego: opened PR #412 to add a collector-side opt-out list (collector config: drop_tag_patterns). Requesting review from infra and SDK teams.

Open hypotheses we want to validate:
- H1: Most of the cost increase is attributable to token tags from one or two client SDK releases (priority: confirm which releases and which clients).
- H2: Applying top-n cardinality guardrails on dashboards reduces incident triage time by 25% without losing actionable signals.
- H3: Pre-aggregation of span histograms will knock down query cost for latency heatmaps by ~60% while keeping visual fidelity.

Notes-to-self / informal fragments:
- Check retention config for: traces longer than 5s — some buckets still defaulting to 90d, probably mis-annotated in templates.
- Follow-up with Kai on the on-call deck re: new sampling thresholds.
- Slack thread #observability: huge thread about spikes, link pinned in OBS-824.

Key measurements observed (staging + prod sampling windows):
- Span count (prod, week-on-week): +28%
- Index cardinality (unique tag keys): +52%
- Billing delta (approx): +$12k/mo if unchanged
- Dashboard render latency (heavy tiles): median 2.1s -> 5.6s under load

Decisions (short):
- Disable token-level tag ingestion by default for non-enterprise customers (rollout plan below).
- Adopt top-10 cardinality guardrail on route-level dashboards as a default template.
- Pilot pre-aggregation pipeline for span-duration histograms in staging this sprint.

Rollout plan (brief):
- Stage 1 (this week): collector config change in staging with drop_tag_patterns enabled; run 72h smoke; observe index keys and alert noise. Owner: Diego.
- Stage 2 (canary customers): enable on two low-risk customers (opt-out available). Owner: Maya + Solutions Eng.
- Stage 3: global default for new customers, existing customers retained unless they opt-in. Docs and migration notes required. Owner: Product + SDK.

Action items (concrete):
action_items: Diego: finish collector PR (#412) and get infra review — target 2027-06-13
Maya: create canary rollout list and coordinate with Solutions Eng for opt-out messaging — due 2027-06-15
Priya: implement dashboard tile guardrail toggle and add to dashboard template library — due 2027-06-17
Omar: extend tail-sampling experiment to include web-inference namespace and report impact by next Wed
Sofia: run pre-aggregation microbenchmark on staging with synthetic traces and share cost delta (expected end 2027-06-18)
Kai (on-call): update runbook entry about log forwarder cert / replays and add a short remediation playbook — due 2027-06-12
decisions: Disable high-cardinality token tags for non-enterprise customers by default (collector-level drop).
Use top-N cardinality guardrail on heavy dashboards to reduce render and cognitive load.
Pilot span-duration pre-aggregation as an intermediate optimization before broader sampling changes.
blockers: Need infra review on PR that touches collector config (security/compat concerns).
SDK team needs time to ship a new release that avoids token tags; until then collector must patch client-side behavior.
Catalog of canary customers not finalized — product needs to sign off on who can be used for Stage 2.
notes_for_followup:
- Confirm which SDK releases introduced token tagging and produce a list of affected client versions.
- Add a small telemetry experiment to split 50/50 traffic on canary to validate guardrail UX.
- Iterate on the runbook to include the new sampling thresholds and the collector toggle steps.
raw_snippets_and_queries:
Example quick queries used during triage:
- count(spans) by service,route over 1h
- topk(10, unique_count(tags.service.route))
- sum(cost_indexed) by day where tag like 'token_%'
(These were run in ad-hoc mode; formalize them into a cost-telemetry workbook.)

Slack refs: #observability, pinned message OBS-824.
Confluence: trace-economics-experiment-notes (linked above).
closing_notes: This doc is an iterative capture. Next sync on 2027-06-14 to review canary metrics and decide Stage 3 timing. If you’re owner on an action, please add progress comments here or on the linked Jira.
